{{Short description|Concept in geometry}}
{{more citations needed|date=April 2016}}

In [[geometry]], a '''quaternionic polytope''' is a generalization of a [[polytope]] in [[real coordinate space|real space]] to an analogous structure in a [[quaternion]]ic [[module (mathematics)|module]], where each real dimension is accompanied by three [[imaginary number|imaginary]] ones. Similarly to [[complex polytope]]s, points are not ordered and there is no sense of "between", and thus a quaternionic polytope may be understood as an arrangement of connected points, lines, planes and so on, where every point is the junction of multiple lines, every line of multiple planes, and so on. Likewise, each line must contain multiple points, each plane multiple lines, and so on. Since the quaternions are non-[[commutative property|commutative]], a convention must be made for the multiplication of vectors by scalars, which is usually in favour of left-multiplication.<ref>{{cite journal| last1 = Hoggar| first1 = S.G.| editor-last1 = Davis| editor-first1 = Chandler | editor1-link = Chandler Davis| editor-last2 = Grünbaum| editor-first2 = Branko| editor2-link = Branko Grünbaum| editor-last3 = Sherk| editor-first3 = F.A.| url = https://books.google.com/books?id=XpDbBwAAQBAJ&dq=quaternionic+polytope&pg=PA219| title = Two Quaternionic 4-polytopes| journal = The Geometric Vein: The Coxeter Festschrift| year = 1980| access-date = 2023-10-31| isbn = 9781461256489| pages = 219–229}}</ref>

As is the case for the complex polytopes, the only quaternionic polytopes to have been systematically studied are the [[regular polytope|regular]] ones. Like the real and complex regular polytopes, their symmetry groups may be described as reflection groups. For example, the regular quaternionic lines are in a one-to-one correspondence with the finite subgroups of ''U''<sub>1</sub>('''H'''): the [[binary cyclic group]]s, [[binary dihedral group]]s, [[binary tetrahedral group]], [[binary octahedral group]], and [[binary icosahedral group]].<ref>{{cite journal|author=Hans Cuypers |title=Regular quaternionic polytopes |date= September 1995|doi=10.1016/0024-3795(95)00149-L |volume=226-228 |pages=311–329 |journal=Linear Algebra and Its Applications|doi-access=free }}</ref>
